chapter_title: Concerning the Summons, in which Limb of the Soul
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶2:** Indeed, the first celestial principle — the Divine Rational as to good — extended itself outward, and it [GAP-1] a particular faculty of the interior spiritual life [GAP-2] of the interior spiritual life; it has [GAP-3] it did not perceive [GAP-4] — but the blessed, glorious Divine-Human principle came [GAP-5: REVIEW in] a hidden manner: in its own form of wisdom; in its own likeness of good; in its own love; in its holy pure affection of truth — she who is the celestial affection of divine truth, the inmost life proceeding from the Divine Love itself.

---

**¶3:** After the manner of the natural body of understanding: as the roots of all derivative faculties depend upon the governing celestial principle, so that should any particular faculty of the spiritual person be severed, while the governing love endures there remains hope for [GAP-6] regeneration — but if the governing celestial love itself should be destroyed, the entire organized spiritual life perishes and is lost utterly.

---

**¶4:** This is also the case for the first celestial principle. It is the governing love, while its derivative goods and truths attach to it as the particular faculties [GAP-7: REVIEW of] its interior life. Or, conversely, like the living sphere of spiritual faith, upon which all natural existence entirely subsists, as it draws in truth and [GAP-8] lives thereby. Its governing love is established upon the whole organized form of the Divine Order — the axis of influx that connects the inmost to the outermost — in the highest states of the universal spiritual world.

---

**¶5:** This is also the case [GAP-9: REVIEW for] the Divine Love, the blessed Divine-Human principle; as it is like the governing celestial love set upon the organized spiritual form, and the sustaining sphere of truth that upon the axis of Divine Order is established i[GAP-10: n] the whole of existence — being confirmed and strengthened by its pure celestial affection of truth, [GAP-11: REVIEW she] who is its inmost life, which it invests with [GAP-12] external truths as garments.

---

**¶6:** [GAP-13] those [GAP-14] interior faculties: the interior rational, the reflective understanding, the perceptive intuition, the deliberative will, and the contemplative judgment — which it brought forth and sent proceeding from itself to accomplish the Divine purpose. The governing principle arose and went forth after them. [GAP-15] — seeking its interior spiritual life, which is entangled and captive among the falsities from evil; as these scattered goods and truths are like the particular faculties of its organized form, and [GAP-16] throughout the whole spiritual world.

---

**¶7:** And when these faculties were sent forth, at that time the governing principle was found conjoined with the pure celestial Affection of Truth, and [GAP-17: REVIEW it] arose, petitioning and entreating for an influx of Divine power. [GAP-18] the Divine bestowed upon it the state of celestial peace and a conj[GAP-19: unction of good with truth] — and it [GAP-20: REVIEW bestowed] upon it the glad perception of Divine truth [GAP-21] concerning the Divine-Human principle. The Divine-Human principle itself gave [GAP-22: its] derivative goods and truths — its particular faculties — and gathered its interior spiritual life i[GAP-23: nto] unity; it built and established that life in its rightful place as an ordered doctrine of truth [GAP-24] — a tower of understanding raised upon its proper foundation.

---

**¶8:** [GAP-25] It formed that doctrine and perfected it with Divine wisdom and skill, [GAP-26] giving it the complete f[GAP-27: orm] of heavenly order — through the Divine truths it sent forth [GAP-28] so that it might penetrate into and subdue [GAP-29] the evil loves that had devastated the interior life — the spiritual life that had been crushed and brought to desolation by the power of falsity from evil. All these scattered goods were gathered inward. They came, and were confirmed and restored once more, into the very likeness of the Divine Love from which they had proceeded.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: “Indeed, the First Man dispersed himself and he [became a] limb of the living soul [and a portion] of the living soul; he has [fallen and] he did not know [... ...] but the blessed, glorious Man came [in] secret; in his image; in his shape; in his love; in his holy virgin, she who is the virgin of light, the soul of the father.

“After the fashion of this fleshly body: as the root of all the limbs hang upon the head, so that should one of the person's limbs be cut off, while the head exists he has hope for [life] but if his head should be cut off, the entire body will die and he is lost.

“This is also the case for the Firs[t] Ma[n]. He is the head, while his sons attach to it the limbs [of] his soul. Or, conversely, like the living air, on which all flesh entirely lives as it breathes and [lives] therein. His head is placed on the body of the Pillar of Glory in the heights of the universe.

“[This i]s also the case [for] the father, the blessed Man; as he is like the head that is upon the body and the air that upon the Pillar is set i[n the universe] being made strong by his light virgin, [she] who is his soul that he clothes [with his light]

“[And also] t[h]ose [five limbs]: the mind, thought, insight, counsel and c[on]sideration that he produced and sent forth from hi[m to] do his will. He sprang and travelled behind them. [He sought the limbs] of his living soul, which is entwined among the rebels; as they are like the limbs of its body, and [spread throughout the] universe.

“And when they were sent, at [that ti]m[e] he was found with the Virgin of [Lig]ht and [he] stood up, asking and entreating for a p[o]wer. [And the father heard him. He] gave him peace and a ki[ss of peace. And] he [gave] him goo[d] tidings [concerning the] Man. The Man him[s]elf gave [his sons and] his limbs and gathered his soul i[nto one. And] he built it in its place like this tower [upon a firm foundation]

“[And he] shaped it and beautified it skillfully [and gave it the] for[m of light. Through] the voices that he sent [forth so that] he might sink in and quench [the fire and save the living] so[u]l that was crushed by the enemy. They were gathered in. They came, set firm once more, in the image of their father.”

fills.explanation: The First Man dispersed himself and thereby became identified with a single limb/faculty of the living soul — reduced from the whole to a mere part, setting up the head-limb analogy developed in ¶3-4.

Parallel construction with "limb of the living soul" — a second descriptor emphasizing the First Man's complete identification with the scattered interior life, matching the spiritual sense of "a particular faculty."

In the Manichaean narrative the First Man fell into unconsciousness after his dispersal; "fallen" directly precedes "did not know," expressing the loss of perception that the spiritual reading identifies.

The editor's "in" is confirmed: "came in secret" is standard Kephalaia phrasing for the hidden manner of the Divine-Human principle's descent, matching the spiritual sense of coming in a concealed way.

In the head-body analogy, if a limb is severed but the head survives, there is hope for life — the natural-register equivalent of the spiritual reading's "regeneration," since life = the possibility of restoration.
The editor's "of" is confirmed: "the limbs of his soul" is the natural possessive construction matching the spiritual "particular faculties of its interior life."
The air analogy requires: all flesh "breathes and lives therein" — the two essential functions of dependence on air, corresponding to the spiritual sense of drawing in truth and living thereby.
The editor's "for" is confirmed: "the case for the father" is the standard Kephalaia construction introducing a parallel application, matching the repeated formula from ¶4.

Completes "in the universe" — the air/truth that is set upon the Pillar is established throughout all existence, paralleling the earlier phrase "in the heights of the universe" and matching the spiritual sense of "the whole of existence."
The editor's "she" is confirmed: the virgin of light is consistently feminine in the Kephalaia, and "she who is his soul" follows the established formula from ¶2.

The father invests his soul-virgin with his light, corresponding to the spiritual sense of clothing the inmost life with external truths as garments — since in the Kephalaia, light = truth and garments = external forms of truth.

Standard Kephalaia transitional phrase introducing a new parallel element — the five intellectual faculties — as an additional aspect of the father's constitution alongside the virgin/soul described in ¶5.

In the Kephalaia, mind, thought, insight, counsel, and consideration are consistently called the "five limbs" — the standard Manichaean term for these interior intellectual faculties, matching the spiritual reading's "interior faculties."

After springing and travelling after the five faculties, the father sought the limbs of his living soul — expressing the active seeking described in the spiritual reading, while maintaining the body-limbs imagery used throughout the chapter.

The scattered goods and truths (soul-limbs) are like body parts and are spread throughout the universe, matching the spiritual reading's "throughout the whole spiritual world" and the chapter's theme of dispersal.
The editor's "he" is confirmed: the First Man is the masculine subject who stood up with the Virgin of Light to petition for divine power.

fills.fill: And the father heard him. He
fills.explanation: In the Manichaean Call and Answer, the First Man entreats and the Divine (Father of Greatness) hears and responds — the spiritual reading's "the Divine bestowed" requires identifying the responding agent, who then gave peace.
Completes "kiss of peace" — the standard Manichaean greeting of salvation representing the conjunction of good with truth — followed by the transitional "And" before the giving of good tidings.
The editor's "gave" is confirmed: "gave him good tidings" is the natural Kephalaia expression for bestowing the glad perception of divine truth upon the rescued First Man.
Connects "good tidings" to "Man" — the tidings concern the Divine-Human principle, using the formal Kephalaia preposition matching the spiritual reading's "concerning the Divine-Human principle."

The Man gave his sons and his limbs — the standard Kephalaia pairing of "sons" (derivative goods) and "limbs" (particular faculties), matching the spiritual reading's "derivative goods and truths — its particular faculties."

Completes "into one" — he gathered his soul into unity, matching the spiritual reading's "gathered its interior spiritual life into unity," followed by "And" transitioning to the building/tower imagery.

The tower simile is completed by its foundation — matching the spiritual reading's "a tower of understanding raised upon its proper foundation," expressed in the Kephalaia's natural architectural register.
Standard Kephalaia paragraph-opening transition continuing the subject (the First Man/father) from the previous paragraph into the new action of shaping and beautifying.
Bridges "skillfully" to "form" — he beautified the doctrine and gave it the complete form, matching the spiritual reading's "giving it the complete form of heavenly order."

Completes "form of light" (the organized structure of divine truth = heavenly order in the spiritual reading), followed by "Through" introducing the instrumental means — the voices/divine truths sent forth.

Completes "sent forth" and introduces the purpose clause "so that he might sink in" — the voices were sent forth as divine truths so that the father might penetrate the darkness, matching the spiritual reading's purpose structure.

fills.fill: the fire and save the living
fills.explanation: In the Kephalaia, "quench" naturally takes "fire" as its object (the burning of evil/the enemy), and the purpose is to save the living soul — matching the spiritual reading's "subdue the evil loves" and "the spiritual life that had been crushed."
